headline: Cytoskeletal mechanics and turnover set force networks in computational cell models
label: Actomyosin Mechanics Cellular Models
summary: Computational preprints now tie actin turnover, filament mechanics and cell deformability to how force is distributed within and between cells.
synthesis: The common thread across these preprints is that cytoskeletal mechanics, specifically filament mechanics, turnover and myosin-driven stress, is treated as the explicit determinant of how force is distributed at subcellular and intercellular scales. A discrete cellular-scale model of the actomyosin cortex reconstructs local surface stress from element forces, linking filament mechanics, turnover and myosin activity to dynamic load-bearing structures. A physics-based model of actin network formation, with orientational filament distribution, strain-dependent depolymerization and actomyosin contribution, is used to explain perinuclear actin structure formation through mechanosensitivity of polymerization. A Fourier Contour Cell study shows that deformability and self-propulsion shape bimodal intercellular contact-force distributions. What is new relative to the broader set of mechanism-to-geometry models is the focus on force transmission, with mechanosensitivity of polymerization or turnover as the controlling variable. All three are computational reproductions, and none reports experimental comparison.
